title: Open-Weight VLM Recipes: What Actually Matters

questions.question: Which set matches the five-axis design space encoded by the recipe lesson?
options: Image encoder, connector, LLM, data mix, and resolution schedule
Tokenizer vocabulary, optimizer, GPU brand, batch norm, and beam width
Only connector depth and prompt length
Audio codec, robot arm, video FPS, OCR engine, and database
questions.explanation: The lesson treats encoder, connector, language model, data mixture, and resolution schedule as separate recipe axes. The other choices mix in unrelated implementation details.

questions.question: In axis_impact, which factor receives the largest share of explained benchmark variance?
options: Connector architecture at 5%
Visual-token count at 60%
Image encoder at 20%
Resolution schedule at 5%
questions.explanation: The controlled-comparison toy assigns 60% to visual-token count, larger than encoder (20%), LLM size (15%), data (10%), or either 5% axis.

questions.question: Which data row has the highest MMMU score in compare_data?
options: LLaVA-Inst-150k at 40.0
+ ShareGPT4V at 42.0
PixMo + Cauldron + more at 47.0
+ Cauldron at 43.0
questions.explanation: The final compare_data row, PixMo + Cauldron + more, reaches 47.0 MMMU. It is higher than PixMo alone at 45.3 and the earlier mixtures at 43.0 or below.

questions.question: For pick_recipe(budget_b=10, task='ocr'), which candidate scores highest under the toy weights?
options: MM1-3B, because the smallest LLM always wins OCR
Idefics2-8B, because Perceiver-64 is the only OCR connector
Cambrian-1-8B, because four encoders guarantee the top DocVQA score
Molmo-7B-D, because its 92.4 DocVQA score dominates the OCR-weighted total
questions.explanation: The OCR weights emphasize DocVQA (1.2). Among recipes at or below 10B, Molmo-7B-D's 92.4 DocVQA score gives it the highest weighted total.

questions.question: Which encoder row wins CV-Bench in compare_encoders?
options: SigLIP + DINOv2 concat with CV-Bench 67.0
CLIP ViT-L/14 @ 336 with CV-Bench 56.0
SigLIP SO400m/14 @ 384 with CV-Bench 60.0
DINOv2 ViT-g/14 @ 224 with CV-Bench 65.0
questions.explanation: The concatenated SigLIP + DINOv2 row reaches 67.0, so it—not standalone DINOv2 at 65.0—wins the table.

questions.question: What conclusion does the connector row support when token count is held constant?
options: A Q-Former always doubles DocVQA relative to an MLP
MLP, Q-Former, and Perceiver are roughly a wash; encoder, tokens, and data deserve earlier ablations
Connector choice accounts for all variance in the benchmark
Connector architecture cannot be changed after the LLM is selected
questions.explanation: The controlled comparison assigns only about 5% to connector architecture and notes similar MLP, Q-Former, and Perceiver results at equal token counts.
